answer: Seeded trust-flow with decay resists sybils: trust originates at a small hand-vetted honest set and propagates along attestation edges, attenuating each hop, so weight depends on short verified paths to the seed — not on internal edge count. A knoll of fakes densely wired to each other sits an ocean away from any seed; their mutual edges only recirculate an echo of near-zero inflow and amplify nothing. Honest identities earn attestations from nodes already close to the seed, so one real edge to the trusted region outweighs thousands of sybil-internal links.
